# openstatus_playbook (Resource)

Manages a playbook: markdown guidance the OpenStatus agent follows when it runs incidents, writes status page updates, schedules maintenance or drafts postmortems.

The built-in slugs (`incident-response`, `status-page`, `maintenance-windows`, `postmortem`) come with a default title and description. If the workspace has already written one, import it instead of creating it, so its content isn't overwritten. Destroying a built-in makes the agent fall back to the OpenStatus default. Any other slug is a custom playbook and needs a `title` and `description`; a workspace can have up to 20 custom playbooks.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Override a built-in playbook. Title and description default to the
# OpenStatus ones; destroying the resource reverts to the OpenStatus default.
# If the workspace already wrote this playbook, import it first (see below).
resource "openstatus_playbook" "incident_response" {
  slug    = "incident-response"
  content = <<-EOT
    # Incident response

    - SEV1: customer-facing outage. Page {{oncall}} immediately.
    - SEV2: degraded service. Post in {{incident_channel}} within 15 minutes.
    - Update the status page every 30 minutes until resolved.
  EOT

  variables = {
    oncall           = "@sre-oncall"
    incident_channel = "#incidents"
  }
}

# A custom playbook needs a title and a description. The agent reads the
# description to decide when to open the playbook.
resource "openstatus_playbook" "vendor_outages" {
  slug        = "vendor-outages"
  title       = "Vendor outages"
  description = "What to do when a third-party provider (payments, email, CDN) is down."
  content     = file("${path.module}/playbooks/vendor-outages.md")
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `content` (String) The playbook in markdown, at most 10000 characters with its variables filled in. `{{name}}` marks a variable. Leading and trailing whitespace is ignored.
- `slug` (String) Identifies the playbook: lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, max 64 characters. Use a built-in slug (`incident-response`, `status-page`, `maintenance-windows`, `postmortem`) to override that playbook. Changing it forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `description` (String) What the playbook covers (1 to 500 characters). The agent reads it to decide when to open the playbook. Required for custom playbooks. For a built-in slug it defaults to the OpenStatus description when the playbook is first written. Removing it from the configuration keeps the current value.
- `title` (String) Name of the playbook (1 to 100 characters). Required for custom playbooks. For a built-in slug it defaults to the OpenStatus title when the playbook is first written. Removing it from the configuration keeps the current value.
- `variables` (Map of String) Values for the `{{name}}` variables in `content`, by name. Names use lowercase letters, digits and underscores; values are at most 500 characters. Every variable must be referenced in `content` and have a non-empty value. A variable referenced in `content` without a value is left as written.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the playbook was first written (RFC 3339).
- `id` (String) Same as `slug`.
- `updated_at` (String) When the playbook was last changed (RFC 3339).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Playbooks are imported by slug.
terraform import openstatus_playbook.incident_response incident-response
```
